newsitem.title: TAIWAN: E.Asia Grains - Taiwan to tender for 108,000T corn.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grains - Taiwan to tender for 108,000T corn.

text.p: Taiwanese importers are expected to tender for up to 108,000 tonnes of corn this week as buyers are apprehensive about a rise in futures prices on the Chicago Board of Trade, dealers said on Monday.

Traders said worries a rally in soybean prices could also lift corn futures on the CBOT may prompt Taiwanese buyers to place tenders. Taiwan's CK Group and the Members Feed Industry Group may buy corn shortly, they said.
"Corn buyers are waiting for better timing to place their tenders," a trader said.
But Japanese importers were hesitant about striking deals for the fourth quarter delivery of U.S. corn this week due to uncertainty over rising premiums in the market, traders said.

"There'll be some deals this week. But people aren't yet willing to purchase aggressively," a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses said. "Shippers' offers are very high, while feed-makers are cautious over acquiring raw materials."

Traders said corn premiums for Japan were quoted between 98-3/4 to 100 U.S. cents a bushel over CBOT September futures, an uncomfortably high level which has already caused a delay in completing deals for the last three months of 1997.

They estimated Japan had so far covered only about a quarter of its U.S. corn needs for that period. Japanese buyers usually finish signing contracts for the period before Japan's Obon holidays in mid-August.
Traders were divided over the future direction of freight rates, with some saying they should soften shortly while others believe they may move up further.

"Freight rates usually come down around this time of the year but it remains uncertain," a trader said. "We might see some deals as cash prices in Chicago have softened somewhat on farmers' sales. Yet we haven't heard yet that Japanese buyers
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about US$11.50 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $22.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized September shipments.
